examples.question_text: A cube has side length $5$ m. Vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ are consecutive corners of its square base. Draw triangle $ABC$ and label all its side lengths using exact values.

A cube has side length $6$ cm. Vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ are consecutive corners of its square base, and $D$ is directly above $C$. Draw triangle $ACD$ and label all its side lengths using exact values.

A right triangular prism has triangular ends $PST$ and $QRU$, with corresponding vertices $P$ and $Q$, $S$ and $R$, and $T$ and $U$. The face $PSRQ$ is a rectangle, and $RU$ is perpendicular to that face. Find the size of $\angle PRU$.

A square pyramid has apex $V$ and square base $JKLM$. $O$ is the centre of the base, $N$ is the midpoint of $JK$, and $VO$ is perpendicular to the base. Write down the size of: (a) $\angle VON$; (b) $\angle VOJ$.

coverage.summary: Authored four examples covering all distinct retained assessment methods. Cube lengths differ from the source; angle examples use renamed vertices because perpendicularity fixes the answer at 90 degrees. Question and solution fields are separate, with editable unshaded triangle diagrams and solution-only annotations. Independent equations align at relation signs without unnecessary phantom equals. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. Assessments remain unchanged and were read only for method classification. Final-size diagram verification and independent example review remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: Source Q1(a), image34, asks for the labelled base triangle. For side length 5 m, AB=BC=5 m and AC=sqrt(25+25)=5sqrt(2) m. The solution diagram correctly places the right angle at B and labels all three sides.
Source Q1(b), image35, uses the base diagonal and a perpendicular vertical edge. AC=sqrt(36+36)=6sqrt(2) cm; AD=sqrt(72+36)=6sqrt(3) cm. CD=6 cm and angle ACD=90 degrees. All diagram labels agree.

Source Q3(b), image37, asks for the angle between a rectangular-face diagonal and its perpendicular edge. RP lies in face PSRQ through R; RU is perpendicular to that face at R. Therefore angle PRU=90 degrees. The extracted triangle correctly marks R.

Source Q7(a)(ii–iii), image41, asks for angles between the perpendicular height and base segments towards a midpoint and a corner. ON and OJ lie in the base through O, so VO is perpendicular to both. Angles VON and VOJ are each 90 degrees; both extracted triangles correctly mark O.
